entrypoints.summary: bcrypt::verify(password, hash) accepts the supplied hash string and reaches split_hash.
HashParts::from_str(hash) is also identified as accepting the affected hash input.

affected_components.role: split_hash validates and parses the bcrypt hash; verification and conversion paths invoke the affected parsing behavior.

code_slices.fixed: The patch changes the guard to reject either non-60-byte or non-ASCII input and return BcryptError::InvalidHash.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The patch documents five parser slice boundaries and adds end-to-end verify and direct split_hash regression-test contracts.
code_slices.vulnerable: The pre-fix validation checked only hash.len() != 60 before split_hash performed fixed byte-range &str slices.

impacts.concept: denial of service of bcrypt-calling process

mitigations.concept: reject non-ASCII bcrypt hash before fixed-offset parsing

relation_candidates.rationale: A multi-byte character spanning one of split_hash's fixed byte boundaries supplies the condition that makes a &str slice invalid.
relation_candidates.src: attacker-controlled 60-byte bcrypt hash containing multi-byte UTF-8

relation_candidates.rationale: The invalid fixed-range slice invokes Rust's string slice boundary failure path.

relation_candidates.dst: denial of service of bcrypt-calling process
relation_candidates.rationale: The advisory scopes the panic's security consequence to denial of service.

relation_candidates.dst: reject non-ASCII bcrypt hash before fixed-offset parsing
relation_candidates.rationale: The patch rejects non-ASCII strings before parser slicing, which ensures fixed offsets only operate on ASCII characters.

sources.concept: attacker-controlled 60-byte bcrypt hash containing multi-byte UTF-8

impact.affected_asset: Availability of the Rust application or service invoking bcrypt::verify or HashParts::from_str.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause a process using the affected API to panic by causing it to process an attacker-controlled malformed, 60-byte non-ASCII hash string.
impact.security_effect: Denial of service through a panic in bcrypt hash parsing or verification.

causal_trace.summary: A caller supplies a 60-byte hash string containing a multi-byte UTF-8 character positioned across a parser byte-slice boundary.

The parser accepted input based on byte length without requiring the valid bcrypt-hash invariant that all 60 bytes are ASCII, leaving fixed byte offsets potentially outside UTF-8 character boundaries.
split_hash performed fixed-range &str slices, including salt_and_hash[..22], across a multi-byte character; Rust rejected that non-character-boundary slice in str::slice_error_fail.
The panic terminates the calling Rust code path, yielding denial of service when an attacker controls the hash passed to the affected APIs.

failure.operation: Fixed-offset &str slicing in split_hash reaches str::slice_error_fail when a range endpoint is inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character.

primary_invariant.kind: bcrypt hash encoding and Rust string-slice boundary invariant
primary_invariant.statement: A valid bcrypt hash is exactly 60 ASCII bytes before split_hash applies fixed byte offsets as &str ranges.
primary_invariant.violated_because: A 60-byte UTF-8 string can contain a multi-byte non-ASCII character that spans one of the fixed byte boundaries while still satisfying the pre-fix length check.

quality.review_notes: Mechanism, patch, historical reproducer, and regression-test intent are artifact-backed. The issue's captured panic is for bcrypt 0.10.0, while the advisory identifies the later regression as versions 0.19.0 through before 0.19.2; the PR/advisory attribute the same boundary-slicing mechanism to that regression. No local test execution or CI run result was supplied, so regression tests are recorded as oracle contracts rather than observed passing results.

remediation.invariant_restored: split_hash rejects hashes whose length is not 60 bytes or whose content is not ASCII, so its fixed parser offsets cannot bisect a multi-byte UTF-8 character.
mitigation_classes: ASCII input validation before fixed-offset string slicing

target.component: hash-string parser used by bcrypt::verify and HashParts::from_str

oracle.expected_negative: The same malformed input must not reach str::slice_error_fail or panic during the parser's fixed-offset slicing.
oracle.expected_positive: A 60-byte hash containing a multi-byte UTF-8 character at the affected offset is rejected with BcryptError::InvalidHash by verify and by split_hash.
